← Getting started · Kitchen sink

Build applications with public kit components

The dashboard layouts now use Colibri's public application component stylesheet. Copy the component markup from the kitchen sink, supply your data and images, and connect your application actions. You do not need dashboard CSS or its rendering scripts.

Buildless HTML

Run the CLI's init command to copy the kit, then include:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="colibri/css/colibri.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="colibri/css/colibri-applications.css">
<body class="colibri-application">
  <main class="app-main">
    <section class="app-card">
      <h1>Your application</h1>
      <p>Render your data here.</p>
    </section>
  </main>
</body>

Bundlers and React

import '@colibri-kit/css';
import '@colibri-kit/css/applications';

These are checkout package entry points; follow the installation guide to install from the repository. Each application example includes a native React component, a parameterized FreeMarker macro, and a Thymeleaf fragment. Their tabs show model data and actual imports or fragment calls. The Java templates render on the server; public browser controllers handle navigation, filtering and chart ranges.

Per-example framework support matrix

Bundle sizes

The application stylesheet is optional and additional to core CSS. These are build measurements; delivered transfer size depends on server compression.

    Framework APIs

    Import the React exports from @colibri-kit/ui/react. Pass model, onAction and onSubmit to application components. The chart accepts rows, labels and range settings directly. Java templates are included in the Java supplement.

    The JavaScript tab supplies working sample handlers. Replace those handlers with your application state and API calls. FreeMarker and Thymeleaf tabs call the packaged templates; they are not HTML copies.

    Components available in the kitchen sink

    • Application shell and mobile navigation
    • Metrics, charts, and record tables
    • Opportunity board
    • Project cards and planner
    • Profile and settings
    • Product collection and store summary
    • Conversation desk
    • Forms, photo features, and articles

    Optional navigation behavior

    Use the shell markup shown in the kitchen sink, with sidebar, trigger, close and backdrop parts. Then initialize:

    import { createApplicationShell } from './colibri/core/application-shell.js';
const navigation = createApplicationShell(document.body);
// navigation.open(); navigation.close(); navigation.destroy();

    The controller manages mobile visibility, inert content, Escape, focus return and keyboard focus containment. It does not create routes or fetch data.

    Customization and ownership

    The stylesheet uses Colibri's --c-* tokens and cascade layers. Set your brand tokens centrally. Use the documented data-layout compositions or combine the core stack, grid, cluster and split primitives. Sample photos are content; provide your own image URLs.

    These are UI components. Your application owns persistence, API requests, authentication, form submission and domain rules. The dashboard demos provide working local sample handlers, not a production backend.
